name: Pumper Bundles
summary: Shopify bundle app by Profit Pumper: unlimited product bundles, quantity breaks, volume and cart discounts, BOGO and free-gift offers, with cart drawer and page builder integrations. The plans are a revenue ceiling rather than a feature ladder: all four carry identical features.
best_for: shopify stores that want bundles, quantity breaks, BOGO and free-gift offers without touching code, and that value a free tier which is the complete app rather than a feature-stripped demo
skip_if: you expect more capability as you pay more (past the first paid step every tier carries the same features and you are only buying a higher revenue ceiling) or you need conditional bundling logic beyond tiered discounts
honest_knock: The paid tiers ship the same features, so what you are buying is a ceiling on the revenue the app is allowed to earn you. The bill therefore rises exactly when the app is working, and it rises in steps: pass $300 and you owe $9.99, pass $1,000 and you owe $29.99, pass $5,000 and you owe $49.99. Read that in both directions. It makes every upgrade past the first buy you nothing new, only permission to keep going. The free plan is smaller than the listing suggests: in our own test on 17 November 2026 it left out Buy X Get Y, Mix and Match, upsells and free shipping goals, and the app calls its $300 a lifetime limit. The one number the pricing table never defines is how that attributed extra revenue is measured, and it is the number the entire ladder rests on.

pricing.plans_source: summarised from pricing.notes; every plan name and amount appears verbatim in those notes
pricing.notes: (read 2026-11-17 on apps.shopify.com/pumper-quantity-breaks-product-bundles-discounts and in our own test the same day; vendor site read 2026-09-19; listed amounts unchanged since 2 September) Four tiers on the listing: Free up to $300 of extra revenue generated by the app, Starter $9.99 a month, Growth $29.99 and Unlimited $49.99, with a 7 day free trial on the paid ones. The paid ladder is priced by how much extra revenue the app is allowed to generate for you: on the listing the feature list, with unlimited bundles and quantity breaks, chat support seven days a week, bundles on page builders and cart drawer integrations, is identical on all four. Inside the app it is not. In our own test on 17 November 2026 the plans were named Build, Scale and Dominate instead of Starter, Growth and Unlimited, Free was described as a “Lifetime limit of $300 in bundle revenue”, and its complete feature list left out free shipping, swatches, subscriptions, market targeting, translation, predefined variants, Mix and Match, Buy X Get Y, upsells, checkbox upsells, the progressive free gift, deal reveal and the countdown timer, all of which the three paid plans include. Free covers up to $300 of extra revenue generated by the app, counted over the life of the store according to the app. Starter is $9.99 a month, or $94.68 a year (saves 21%), and covers up to $1,000. Growth is $29.99 a month or $269.88 a year (save 25%) and covers up to $5,000. Unlimited is $49.99 a month or $449.88 a year (save 25%) and removes the ceiling. Charges are billed in USD every 30 days. Two things on the vendor's own site contradict the listing and were unresolved on 19 September 2026: its FAQ says the trial is 14 days with full access and no card, against the listing's 7 days (Shopify's own approval screen showed 7 days in our test on 17 November 2026); and it answers 'Are there any hidden charges?' by saying Pumper charges a maximum of $39.99 a month, against the listing's $49.99 top tier. Where the two differ, the listing is the page Shopify bills from. Neither page defines how the attributed extra revenue that decides your tier is measured. The vendor trades as Profit Pumper (Henq eCommerce LLC, Delaware).

compare_with.name: AfterSell
compare_with.why: These sit at opposite ends of the same funnel: Pumper Bundles works before the buy (bundles, quantity breaks, BOGO and free-gift offers on the product page and in the cart) while AfterSell works after it, on the post-purchase and thank-you pages. Plenty of stores run both. If you are picking one, pick by where your AOV problem actually is: shoppers who never add a second item, or completed orders you never follow up on. On price Pumper is the cheaper entry, and its free tier covers volume discounts and bundles up to $300 of attributed revenue.

exit_test.what: The app was installed on our Shopify development store, which we set up, and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 17 November 2026 the session tested Pumper Bundles on a Shopify development store: the install, the Free plan without a card, a Volume Discount template that gave a Live Preview with Buy 2 10% off and Buy 3 20% off about 1 minute 10 seconds and 4 steps after the install click, the plan page, the Shopify approval screen for Build (a 7-day trial; it said there would be no test charge but asked for a payment method; nothing approved) and the uninstall dialog, after which the app was uninstalled. The offer was not published, so it was not seen on a real product page. Nothing was paid. Install: the Install button on the App Store listing (apps.shopify.com/pumper-quantity-breaks-product-bundles-discounts, English, vendor Profit Pumper Bundle) was clicked in our own tab at 20:37 and the form led straight to the Shopify screen Install app in the same tab. The screen said the app needs access to View customer data (Device and activity data), View staff and contributor data (Store owner) and View and edit store data (Customers, products, orders, discounts, Online Store, custom data, Shopify admin). Install was confirmed and the app opened on Choose your plan. No vendor account, password, Google login or terms tick box was seen, and no call or phone number was asked. Core action, a volume discount: Select Free Plan (No charges - Free forever) gave the toast Plan Activated with no Shopify approval screen. The app then showed Offer templates (Every card is the real storefront widget, mounted with that template's settings) with templates such as Volume Discount, Buy X Get Y, Mix & Match, Bundle, Progressive Free Gift and Side-by-Side Packs. One click on Use this template at Volume Discount opened the editor Offer 1 with the tiers Buy 1, Buy 2 and Buy 3, Show on All products and a Live Preview next to it. For the product The Complete Snowboard the Live Preview said Buy More Save More, Buy 1 Standard Price $699.95, Buy 2 10% OFF Save $139.98 $1,259.92 (was $1,399.90) and Buy 3 20% OFF Save $419.97 $1,679.88 (was $2,099.85), with the badge Most Popular. The first result stood there about 1 minute 10 seconds after the install click (20:37 to about 20:38) and 4 steps in all (confirm the install, Select Free Plan, Use this template; nothing had to be filled in). A line under the preview said Remove Powered by Pumper by offer verification, and a chat bubble asking Need any help setting up the offer? with a photo of an agent was in the corner (hidden in the images, not opened). The offer was not published and not saved (Publish and Save as draft were not used) and no theme change was made, so whether the widget shows on a real product page was NOT tested. Plans in the app (Monthly; the Yearly button says Up to 25% Off): Free $0.00 a month with Lifetime limit of $300 in bundle revenue and No charges - Free forever; Build $9.99 a month with Up to $1,000 extra sales for your store and the button Start 7-days trial; Scale $29.99 a month (Most Popular) with Up to $5,000 extra sales; Dominate $49.99 a month with Unlimited extra sales; under the paid plans Full money-back guarantee. Cancel anytime. After the Free plan was activated the Plans page said Current Plan Free and Earned $0 / $300. The Complete feature list is not the same on every plan: Free has crosses for Free shipping, Swatches, Subscription, Target by market, Translation, Predefined variants, Mix & Match deals, Buy X Get Y deals, Upsell, Checkbox upsell, Progressive free gift, Deal reveal and Countdown timer, and ticks for Free gift, Add image, Sold out tier, Bundle deals and Animated border; Build, Scale and Dominate have everything ticked. Checkout: Start 7-days trial on Build (monthly) opened the Shopify screen Approve subscription: a yellow bar You will not be billed for this test charge., the plan Build (monthly), $9,99 USD every 30 days, You have a 7-day free trial ending on 24 Nov., Subtotal $9,99 plus any applicable taxes, Total $9,99 Due 24 Nov, and a row Add payment method (so no payment method was stored), with By proceeding, you are agreeing to the Terms of Service. The Approve button looked active, but it was not clicked because a payment method was being asked and no card may be entered; Cancel was clicked and nothing was approved. Cancelling: no subscription ran. Removing the app goes through Settings, Apps, the menu of the app and Uninstall: the dialog Uninstall Pumper Bundles? says that you can no longer use the app, that data managed by the app, such as discounts, will be deleted and that a request goes to the app developer within 48 hours to delete all personal customer information; a reason had to be chosen (Testing multiple apps) before the uninstall. Differences from the review: the listing names the plans Starter, Growth and Unlimited and the app names them Build, Scale and Dominate, with the same prices ($9.99, $29.99 and $49.99); the review and the listing say that every plan has the same features, while in the app Free lacks Free shipping, Mix & Match, Buy X Get Y, Upsell, Translation and Countdown timer among others; the review says Free is the full app up to $300 of extra revenue, while the app says Lifetime limit of $300 in bundle revenue; the review says the vendor site gives a 14 day trial against 7 days on the listing, and the Shopify screen and the plan buttons said 7 days (the vendor site was not opened). The price fields are not changed here. Not tested: publishing the offer and the widget on a real product page, Mix & Match, Buy X Get Y, upsell and Free shipping (not on the Free plan and no paid plan was activated), rule-based bundles, how the extra revenue is measured, Analytics (Beta) and the chat. Clean up: the app was uninstalled at about 20:41 through Settings, Apps (message: You have successfully uninstalled Pumper Bundles). No offer was saved, no theme change was made, no test product was made and no card was entered. Our own tab was closed. No kit records were entered.
exit_test.awkward: The Complete feature list differs per plan although the listing says the features are the same; the Free plan has a lifetime limit of $300 in bundle revenue; the approval screen said there would be no test charge but still asked for a payment method; and the plan names in the app differ from the listing.

Install was confirmed and the app opened on Choose your plan. No vendor account, password, Google login or terms tick box was seen, and no call or phone number was asked. Cancel anytime. After the Free plan was activated the Plans page said Current Plan Free and Earned $0 / $300. The Complete feature list is not the same on every plan: Free has crosses for Free shipping, Swatches, Subscription, Target by market, Translation, Predefined variants, Mix & Match deals, Buy X Get Y deals, Upsell, Checkbox upsell, Progressive free gift, Deal reveal and Countdown timer, and ticks for Free gift, Add image, Sold out tier, Bundle deals and Animated border; Build, Scale and Dominate have everything ticked. Checkout: Start 7-days trial on Build (monthly) opened the Shopify screen Approve subscription: a yellow bar You will not be billed for this test charge., the plan Build (monthly), $9,99 USD every 30 days, You have a 7-day free trial ending on 24 Nov., Subtotal $9,99 plus any applicable taxes, Total $9,99 Due 24 Nov, and a row Add payment method (so no payment method was stored), with By proceeding, you are agreeing to the Terms of Service. The Approve button looked active, but it was not clicked because a payment method was being asked and no card may be entered; Cancel was clicked and nothing was approved. Cancelling: no subscription ran. Removing the app goes through Settings, Apps, the menu of the app and Uninstall: the dialog Uninstall Pumper Bundles? says that you can no longer use the app, that data managed by the app, such as discounts, will be deleted and that a request goes to the app developer within 48 hours to delete all personal customer information; a reason had to be chosen (Testing multiple apps) before the uninstall. The price fields are not changed here. Not tested: publishing the offer and the widget on a real product page, Mix & Match, Buy X Get Y, upsell and Free shipping (not on the Free plan and no paid plan was activated), rule-based bundles, how the extra revenue is measured, Analytics (Beta) and the chat. Clean up: the app was uninstalled at about 20:41 through Settings, Apps (message: You have successfully uninstalled Pumper Bundles). No offer was saved, no theme change was made, no test product was made and no card was entered. Our own tab was closed. No kit records were entered.
